purpose: Two independent real IonQ ionq_simulator submissions of the EXACT SAME iteration-15 tapered circuit (z2_tapered_ionq.py, generic StatePreparation, mean 3.94 CX, 3-qubit reduced register), to check whether the abstract-vs-tapered real-hardware gap is a reproducible structural effect or an artifact of limited (10,000) shot statistics from a single submission.
conclusion: run1 and run2 agree within roughly their combined statistical uncertainty (aria-1: 47.78 vs 50.28, diff=2.50, combined std~2.83; forte-1: 51.25 vs 55.24, diff=3.99, combined std~2.13, slightly outside 1-sigma but nowhere near closing the ~12-15 kcal/mol gap to the abstract ansatz). CONFIRMED: the tapered-vs-abstract real-hardware gap is a real, reproducible effect across independent submissions, not shot-noise luck from a single draw at 10,000 shots.
